Physics: All forty keys check out on recomputation, and the topic spread is broad and reasonably balanced between Class 11 and Class 12 with no genuine content duplication. The difficulty, however, is skewed low: apart from Q6, Q16, Q17 and Q37, almost every item is a one-formula substitution (Q1, Q3, Q8, Q10, Q11, Q30, Q31, Q34, Q40), which is easier than the typical BITSAT mix. Swap a handful of the pure recall items for two- or three-concept problems (e.g. combined circuit–diode, interference-with-slab, or energy-plus-rotation) and fix the small wording ambiguities noted above.

[minor] "First half of a journey" is ambiguous between half the distance and half the time, and the half-time reading gives exactly the distractor 10 m s⁻¹ (option C), so state "first half of the distance" explicitly.

[minor] The stem is clumsily worded ("an ideal gas of fixed molecular diameter; for the diatomic gas mentioned below"), leaving it unclear whether all four statements refer to the same diatomic gas; recast as "An ideal diatomic gas with fixed molecular diameter and inactive vibrational modes…" (the physics and key C are correct).
[major] A bare 50 °F → 10 °C conversion is a single school-level arithmetic step well below BITSAT standard; replace it with a faulty-thermometer/scale-calibration or expansion-based item.

[minor] The bracketed double-ratio phrasing ("radiation pressure on the reflecting surface / pressure on the absorbing surface; incident-wave momentum density in the two setups") is convoluted; ask plainly for the two ratios in a stated order (key B is correct).
[minor] Option (A) is written as "1I", which is unidiomatic alongside 9I/4I and should simply read "I".

Chemistry: The section covers the syllabus broadly and the difficulty is pitched correctly for BITSAT: most items are single-step calculations (47, 50, 55, 59–61, 68, 69, 73) or clean recall, all solvable well inside 90 s, and every key I could check independently is correct. Balance is slightly skewed towards VSEPR/hybridisation (42, 48, 72) and unpaired-electron counting (44, 63, 77), while several items (45, 71, 80) are pure one-line recall; thinning the two clusters would free slots for a thermodynamics/ionic-equilibrium or organic-mechanism item. Apart from the sign-convention ambiguity in q64, the only caution is that the figure-based items (42, 49, 54, 56, 58, 62, 78) could only be checked for internal consistency with their options and keys.
[minor] This item tests the same hybridisation/VSEPR-assignment skill as q42 (with q72 on bond angles adding a third VSEPR-type item), so one of them should be swapped for different p-block content.

[minor] The stem does not state whether "increasing order" refers to signed ΔegH values or to the magnitude of energy released, making option D (Ne < Ca < S < Cl) defensible as the exact reverse of the key; add "(signed values, most negative first)".
[minor] Writing the d^n configuration and counting unpaired electrons is essentially the same task already required in q63 (and partly in q44), so this item is redundant and should be replaced.

English Proficiency: The section covers the expected BITSAT English spread (para jumbles, idiom, voice, error spotting, vocabulary, antonym/synonym, analogy and a two-question RC set), and the keys are correct apart from the formatting damage in Q84. Difficulty is skewed easy: Q89 is a two-part shuffle with impossible distractors, and Q82, Q90 and Q92 are near-giveaways, while four items lean on the same error-spotting/improvement format. Fix Q84's duplicated options, rebuild Q89 with four parts, and replace one straightforward grammar item or one literal RC question with an inference/vocabulary-in-context question to lift the overall level.
[minor] In S the village lights appear "below us" although the party is climbing to a remote hill village, a small logical inconsistency with the ascent described in 1, P and R.

[major] The options are printed twice in two incompatible sets (first A = "were prepared...", then A = "The list of items..."), and the stem repeats option A, so the intended key B points to different text depending on which list the candidate reads.
[minor] The item is tagged "Sentence Completion (vocabulary)" but is actually a word-analogy question, so the label must be corrected to Analogy.

[major] With only two movable parts and distractors C and D that reinsert the fixed sentences 1 and 4, the item is trivially easy and its options are structurally invalid for a para-jumble; it needs four jumbled parts.

Logical Reasoning: The type mix (visual, verbal, analytical) is sensible and the keys for the verifiable items (97, 99, 101, 104, 105) are correct, but the section is pitched too low: Q98, Q100, Q105 and to a lesser extent Q99 are single-step, sub-20-second questions with no genuine reasoning load. Q96 cannot be printed at all without its artwork, and the figure-dependent Q102/Q103 must be re-checked against the final diagrams. Swap two of the trivial items for a multi-step arrangement or puzzle-based question to bring the section up to BITSAT difficulty.
[major] All four option figures are blank (no artwork supplied or referenced), so the item is unanswerable and the key D cannot be verified.
[minor] The code is a plain A=1…Z substitution stated in the stem, making this a ~10-second recall task well below BITSAT level; add a twist (e.g., reversed positions or a shift) to raise the demand.
[minor] The stem hands over the classification rule ("three ... name fruits"), reducing the item to spotting a vegetable; delete the rule and let candidates infer the category themselves.
[minor] Five words are listed but only four appear as options ("transact" is omitted), an inconsistent presentation; either offer all five or drop the unused word from the list.
[minor] This tests the same simple alphabet-position stepping as Q98 (and is equally trivial); replace one of the two with a non-alphabet-counting analogy to avoid redundancy.

Mathematics: All 45 keys check out on recomputation, and the spread across calculus, algebra, coordinate geometry, 3D and probability is broadly BITSAT-appropriate, with most items solvable in under 90 seconds. The main structural flaw is the repeated "area bounded by parabola and line" skill (q114, q150), and conics is confined to circles and one parabola with no ellipse or hyperbola. A few items (q117, q140, q147) are single-formula substitutions, so replacing one of them with a moderately harder conic or trigonometry item would sharpen the section's difficulty gradient.
[minor] The options write the answer as a nested pair "$((3,-2),5)$", which is awkward notation; state the choices as "centre $(3,-2)$, radius $5$" etc.

[minor] The stem prescribes "splitting its third row as a sum", but $(7,19,52)$ has no natural decomposition, so this textbook-style method hint is misleading and should be deleted (the determinant is simply evaluated).

[major] This duplicates q114: both ask only for the area of a region bounded by a parabola and a straight line, so one of the two should be replaced (e.g. by an ellipse/hyperbola or a different integration application).
